newsitem.title: USA: Ford adds natural gas vehicles to corporate fleet.
newsitem.headline: Ford adds natural gas vehicles to corporate fleet.

text.p: MCN Corp and Ford Motor Co said Tuesday they will invest more than $500,000 to add 150 natural gas vehicles to Ford's Southeast Michigan corporate fleet.

MCN's MichCon gas distribution subsidiary will install a natural gas fueling station and deliver the gas to Ford's Research and Engineering Center in Dearborn to support the addition of the natural gas vehicles to Ford's fleet.

The companies said 85 percent of Ford's natural gas fleet vehicles will be dedicated to natural gas, while the remaining 15 percent will be bi-fuel vehicles that can run on either natural gas or unleaded gasoline.
Groundbreaking on the new station is scheduled to begin in August and be completed by November. There are now more than 1,000 natural gas fueling stations in the United States, MichCon said.

"Ford has been committed to developing high-quality natural gas vehicles for more than a decade," Ford Chairman Alex Trotman said in a statement. "Now we're bringing that commitment home in a more concrete way by having our own employees drive them on the job on a regular basis."

Ford is offering six natural gas-powered vehicles for the 1998 model year -- a dedicated gas Crown Victoria sedan, F-250 pickup and Econoline van and a bi-fuel Contour sedan, F-series truck and Econoline van. In addition, the natural-gas Crown Victoria is sold as a police package around the country and is newly available in a taxi package with extended range.
